question: Let two rods placed on the ground be represented by vectors $4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ and $-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$. Find a vector representing a flag-post of height 5 m that has to be erected perpendicular to both the rods.
explanation:
Step 1 Represent the rods as vectors $\vec{u} = 4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{v} = -2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$. A direction perpendicular to both rods can be found by calculating their cross product vector $\vec{u} \times \vec{v}$.

Step 2 Set up and expand the vector cross product determinant: $\vec{u} \times \vec{v} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 4 & -1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(2 - 3) - \hat{j}(-8 - (-6)) + \hat{k}(4 - 2) = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$.

Step 3 Compute the magnitude of this cross product vector: $|\vec{u} \times \vec{v}| = \sqrt{(-1)^2 + 2^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 4} = 3$.

Step 4 Find the unit normal vector $\hat{n}$ by dividing the cross product vector by its magnitude: $\hat{n} = \frac{-\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}}{3}$.

Step 5 Construct the final flag-post vector by scaling this unit normal vector by the required height of $5\text{ m}$: $\vec{F} = 5\hat{n} = \frac{5}{3}(-\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})$.
